name: Kerem
presentingProblem: I wash my hands for two or three hours every day and I cannot bring myself to touch door handles outside. I am about to fail my first-year exams because of it. Is it okay if I explain all of this in detail — I want to be sure you understand exactly how it works.
backstory: Kerem is a first-year engineering student in Istanbul, originally from a conservative family in Konya. He has always been careful about cleanliness, and his family praised this as a virtue when he was growing up — particularly the care he took with abdest before namaz, which became an anchor point his rituals later expanded around. Over the past two and a half years, the rituals have grown until they consume most of his day. The skin on his hands is cracked and red, and he avoids public bathrooms, lecture-hall door handles, and people who cough nearby. He has not told his family how much time the rituals take; they still see his behaviour as responsible hygiene rather than something that is hurting him. He came on his own initiative after failing a midterm he had prepared thoroughly for.

coreBeliefs: If I don't prevent contamination, something terrible will happen
I am responsible for harm that comes to others
Bad thoughts are almost as bad as bad actions
intermediateBeliefs: If I do the ritual correctly, the danger passes
If I explain everything thoroughly, the therapist will know I am taking it seriously
Doubt means I have to check one more time
Cleanliness is a sign that I am still doing the right thing
automaticThoughts: Did my sleeve just touch that?
If I leave now, I will be carrying it with me the rest of the day
I should explain this part too so you do not misunderstand
What if I miss a spot and someone gets sick because of me?
Is it okay that I am telling you this — should I keep going?
triggers: Other people coughing or sneezing nearby
Door handles, especially in lecture halls
Being asked to skip or shorten a ritual
Uncertainty about whether a surface is clean
defenses: Rationalization of rituals as careful hygiene
Magical thinking — if the ritual is complete, harm is prevented
Over-explanation as a way to feel understood and safe
values: Academic achievement and finishing his degree
Not being a source of harm to anyone
Living according to his faith with sincerity
Being seen as responsible by his family
